citations.assessment: The direct ruling on a diversionary deed names Chanilai bar Idi transmitting from Shmuel.
The direct orphan property rule names the same transmitter.
The direct young-son statement names Chanilai bar Idi in Shmuel’s name.
The direct witness reads Nehilai bar Idi. Record this variant without asserting Heilprin’s proposed substitution.
The exact Yoma passage also reads Nehilai bar Idi in Shmuel’s name. This is separate from Heilprin’s proposed Chanilai form.

evidence.witness: Babylonian Talmud, Yoma 22b, Wikisource digital transcription

holds.raw: ר' יעקב אחיו, בזמן ר' יוחנן, ר"ל ר' יעקב היה תלמיד ר"י
holds.reason: The text explicitly restricts the studenthood claim to Yaakov. The named Shmuel reports place Chanilai in their transmission chains without attesting the brother relationship.

holds.raw: ר' נהולאי בר אידי אמר שמואל נראה דצ"ל חנילאי
holds.reason: Both named sources read Nehilai. Keep the received Neholai and Heilprin’s proposed Chanilai separate.

notes.text: The three Shmuel reports say Chanilai bar Idi. The checked Taanit and Yoma say Nehilai. Retain Heilprin’s formulation and the express restriction of the studenthood claim to Yaakov.
